title: Elon Musk: "Probably none of us will have a job." Here's what to do instead
text:
"Probably none of us will have a job." Elon Musk, VivaTech, May 2024.
"Whole classes of jobs going away." Sam Altman, The Gentle Singularity, June 2025.

By 2030, employers expect 92 million jobs to be displaced and 170 million new ones created (World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025). Nobody knows which jobs will last, not even the people building AI. So don't bet your future on a job title. Test it first.

title: The jobs employers expect to shrink by 2030 (and what to do instead)
text:
Employers expect bank tellers, data entry clerks, postal service clerks, cashiers, administrative assistants, and accountants and auditors to be among the fastest-declining jobs by 2030, while big data, fintech, AI and machine learning, software and security roles grow fastest (World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025).

And about 60% of US jobs are types of work created since 1940 (MIT research, Quarterly Journal of Economics). New work keeps being invented, so the job you'll love might not have a name yet. Don't choose a job title. Find the kind of work you're good at, then test it.
